bibl.title: Thalamic and extrathalamic mechanisms of consciousness after severe brain injury

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: At a circuit level, the implication of our findings is that, at least in the context of DOC, different aspects of consciousness, including willful behavior and arousal, might be mediated by thalamic and extrathalamic mechanisms, respectively.

span.label: disorders of consciousness after severe brain injury
span.quote: In this cross-sectional study, we recruited a consecutive sample of 143 patients who survived severe brain injury and developed a disorder of consciousness.

span.label: observational-study
span.quote: Methods: Structural T1-weighted magnetic resonance images were collected, in a continuous sample of 143 severely brain-injured patients with DOC (and 96 volunteers), across 2 tertiary expert centers.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Willful behaviour and arousal are supported by separate circuits, so thalamic damage removes organised willful behaviour while extrathalamic (basal ganglia) damage removes behavioural and electrocortical arousal
span.quote: At a circuit level, the implication of our findings is that, at least in the context of DOC, different aspects of consciousness, including willful behavior and arousal, might be mediated by thalamic and extrathalamic mechanisms, respectively.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Loss of corticopetal thalamo-prefrontal projections (the mesocircuit) removes the drive that sustains organised behaviour and integrates information across cortex
span.quote: On the one hand, the negative association between motor/communication scores and atrophy along the anterior and dorsomedial regions of thalamus is consistent with the mesocircuit theory according to which corticopetal projections from thalamus to prefrontal cortex are crucial for sustaining organized behavior26 and integrating information across different regions of cortex.29

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Partial basal forebrain atrophy spares the coma-inducing threshold but impairs the fast cortical disinhibition that transiently amplifies sensory processing
span.quote: comalike state seen in animal models upon complete lesion of this region,18 but might nonetheless have been sufficient to affect the mechanisms of fast cortical disinhibition.

span.label: Structural neuroimaging is descriptive, so the findings cannot be given a causal interpretation
span.quote: Furthermore, the use of structural neuroimaging, a descriptive methodology, to pinpoint neuroanatomical components of consciousness, as measured with standard clinical methods, does not allow a causal interpretation of our findings.

span.label: The atlas-based segmentation relies on priors estimated mostly from healthy volunteers
span.quote: Second, the atlas-based component of our approach is both an asset, allowing improved estimation and segmentation of individual regions, and a liability, given its reliance on priors estimated mostly from healthy volunteers.

span.label: The proposed model is an approximation that omits corticosubcortical connectivity, temporal dynamics, neurotransmitter action and further arousal-related regions
span.quote: Third, it should also be noted that our proposal, as well as the mesocircuit model of DOC,7 are to be understood as approximations that do not take into full account the extent of corticosubcortical connectivity, temporal dynamics,56 the multiple mechanisms of action of neurotransmitters, and a number of additional regions known to be important for the regulation of arousal and cortical function.34

span.label: Additional clinical factors that shape a given patient's atrophy pattern could not be addressed and would need larger samples
span.quote: Nonetheless, it must be recognized that there are a number of additional factors that might well play an important role in determining the specific pattern of atrophy observed in a given patient that we could not address (eg, whether pharmacologic coma was used, the presence of some patients undergoing steroid administration) and that will likely require even larger samples than the present one to allow full statistical evaluation.

span.label: A structure the literature calls crucial could not be assessed by the technique used.
span.quote: parabrachial/precoeruleus complex, which has been previously shown to be crucial for this process (but could not be assessed with the present technique

span.label: The outcome analysed is a set of rotated components, not the clinical subscales themselves.
span.quote: However, because of the correlations between CRS-R subscales, and the negative effects of excessive multicollinearity on regression analysis,20 we performed a data reduction (principal component analysis

span.label: One region entered the analysis on the strength of evidence from animal models.
span.quote: This region was added to the analysis because of its causal role in the maintenance of cortical (and behavioral) arousal in animal models

span.label: a multiple-regression approach across a deliberately HETEROGENEOUS patient sample, controlling the factors known to drive variability in disorders of consciousness
span.quote: employing a multiple regression approach to control for a number of factors that are known to be important sources of variability in DOC

span.label: the region set - BOUNDED BY THE INSTRUMENT, NOT BY THE BIOLOGY: one structure previously shown to be crucial for the process under study could not be assessed with the technique used, so the map of which regions matter is drawn from the regions the method can see
span.quote: parabrachial/precoeruleus complex, which has been previously shown to be crucial for this process (but could not be assessed with the present technique

span.label: the clinical outcome - COMPONENTS, NOT SUBSCALES: the six CRS-R subscales are correlated, so a principal component analysis with varimax rotation was performed and the regression is run on the components; every later claim linking a region to a function is a claim about a component
span.quote: However, because of the correlations between CRS-R subscales, and the negative effects of excessive multicollinearity on regression analysis,20 we performed a data reduction (principal component analysis

span.label: the basal forebrain's role - ESTABLISHED ELSEWHERE, MEASURED HERE: the paper reports its own negative association with sensory responsiveness and, in the next clause, that the region is well known to play a causal role in arousal and to induce a comalike state when extensively lesioned - the causal claim is inherited, the association is measured
span.quote: In addition, we also found that the basal forebrain was (negatively) associated with the degree of sensory responsiveness of patients. This region is well known to play a causal role in the maintenance of behavioral and electrocortical arousal, and to induce a comalike state when extensively lesioned

span.label: builds-on → the mesocircuit theory of disorders of consciousness
span.quote: On the one hand, the negative association between motor/communication scores and atrophy along the anterior and dorsomedial regions of thalamus is consistent with the mesocircuit theory according to which corticopetal projections from thalamus to prefrontal cortex are crucial for sustaining organized behavior26 and integrating information across different regions of cortex.29

span.label: replicates → postmortem examinations of thalamic damage after nontraumatic brain injury
span.quote: Third, paralleling postmortem examinations,50 we have also shown in vivo that patients suffering from nontraumatic brain injury exhibit a more widespread and left-lateralized degree of thalamic atrophy, consistent with the well-known poorer prognosis associated with nontraumatic etiology.1

span.label: basal forebrain —causes→ arousal
span.quote: In addition, we also found that the basal forebrain was (negatively) associated with the degree of sensory responsiveness of patients. This region is well known to play a causal role in the maintenance of behavioral and electrocortical arousal, and to induce a comalike state when extensively lesioned

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: we performed a data reduction (principal component analysis [PCA], with varimax rotation of the loading matrix21) over the CRS-R subscales.

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: Significance was established with nonparametric permutation testing against an a-criterion of 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons using a familywise cluster correction using FSL Randomise module.22,23

span.label: multiple regression
span.quote: Finally, we also note that we have focused on the idea of a “minimum common denominator” across a heterogeneous sample of patients, employing a multiple regression approach to control for a number of factors that are known to be important sources of variability in DOC.

span.label: t-statistic
span.quote: Colored regions indicate areas of significant atrophy in patients (t statistic), collapsing across diagnoses, as compared to healthy volunteers (warmer colors indicate greater atrophy).

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Compared to volunteers, patients exhibited significant atrophy across all structures (p < 0.05, corrected).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: As shown in Figure 3A, the CRS-R total score (analysis #2) correlated inversely with atrophy in large portions of the left globus pallidus (76% of vertices), left putamen (85% of vertices), and small sections of the bilateral ventromedial basal forebrain (8% and 2% of right and left vertices, respectively; Fig 4C).

span.label: Bayesian estimation
span.quote: The segmentation is achieved by incorporating, in a Bayesian framework, individual subject MR image intensities and a set of priors for each target region derived from manual labeling in a set of 336 T1- weighted MR images.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: ranging from 18 to 80 years of age (mean 5 33 years, standard deviation 5 18 years), with no known history of brain disorders

span.label: Compared with healthy volunteers, patients with disorders of consciousness showed significant atrophy in every subcortical structure examined.
span.quote: Compared to healthy volunteers (ie, analysis #1), patients exhibited significant atrophy across all examined regions.

span.label: The behaviourally defined diagnostic categories were not distinguishable by subcortical pathology: vegetative-state, MCS-minus and MCS-plus patients did not differ from one another in any region.
span.quote: No significant differences were detected in the comparison of VS versus MCS2 patients, VS versus MCS1 patients, and MCS2 versus MCS1 patients.

span.label: Total CRS-R score varied inversely with atrophy in the left globus pallidus, left putamen and small ventromedial parts of the basal forebrain.
span.quote: As shown in Figure 3A, the CRS-R total score (analysis #2) correlated inversely with atrophy in large portions of the left globus pallidus (76% of vertices), left putamen (85% of vertices), and small sections of the bilateral ventromedial basal forebrain (8% and 2% of right and left vertices, respectively; Fig 4C).

span.label: Motor and communication ability tracked thalamic pathology: the Motor-Communication component correlated negatively with atrophy in bilateral anterior and dorsomedial thalamus, left putamen and right hippocampus.
span.quote: Motor–Communication component scores exhibited a significant negative correlation with the degree of atrophy in bilateral anterior and dorsomedial thalamus (61% and 27% of vertices in the left and right hemisphere, respectively), small segments of left putamen (36% of vertices), and right medial and posterolateral hippocampus (25% of vertices; see Fig 3C).

span.label: Arousal tracked basal ganglia rather than thalamic pathology: the Arousal component correlated negatively with atrophy in bilateral putamen and globus pallidus.
span.quote: The Arousal component was negatively associated with extensive atrophy in bilateral putamen (69% and 63% in left and right hemisphere, respectively), globus pallidus (92% and 16% of vertices), and a small segment of left posterior hippocampus (3% of vertices; see Fig 3D).

span.label: Arousal showed no association with thalamic atrophy, contrary to the traditional view of thalamic intralaminar nuclei as the arousal-critical structure.
span.quote: More surprising is the absence of association between patients’ level of arousal and thalamic atrophy.

span.label: Sensory (audiovisual) responsiveness was associated specifically with atrophy of small ventromedial segments of the basal forebrain.
span.quote: The Audiovisual component was negatively associated with the degree of atrophy in small bilateral ventromedial segments of the basal forebrain (3% and 5% of vertices in the left and right hemisphere, respectively; see Fig 4D).

span.label: Patients with nontraumatic injury had more widespread and left-lateralised thalamic atrophy than patients with traumatic injury, mirroring the worse prognosis of nontraumatic aetiology.
span.quote: Third, paralleling postmortem examinations,50 we have also shown in vivo that patients suffering from nontraumatic brain injury exhibit a more widespread and left-lateralized degree of thalamic atrophy, consistent with the well-known poorer prognosis associated with nontraumatic etiology.1

span.label: The only clinical-group contrast that reached significance was between the two extremes of the spectrum, with vegetative-state patients showing more left putamen, globus pallidus and right hippocampal atrophy than patients emerging from MCS.
span.quote: Consistent with the result reported for total CRS-R, VS patients exhibited, as compared to eMCS, significant atrophy in left putamen (85% of vertices) and globus pallidus (69% of vertices), as well as in small sections in medial and anterior right hippocampus (6% of vertices).

span.label: shape (or vertex) analysis
span.quote: To assess local brain atrophy on the basis of T1-weighted MR images, we employed a technique referred to as "shape (or vertex) analysis,"12 available in FMRIB Software Library (FSL).13

span.label: "minimum common denominator" of pathology across a heterogeneous DOC sample
span.term: "minimum common denominator" of pathology across a heterogeneous DOC sample
span.quote: Finally, we also note that we have focused on the idea of a “minimum common denominator” across a heterogeneous sample of patients, employing a multiple regression approach to control for a number of factors that are known to be important sources of variability in DOC.

span.label: total CRS-R score (clinical measure of consciousness)
span.term: total CRS-R score (clinical measure of consciousness)
span.quote: Second, we assessed the relationship between total CRS-R score and local atrophy (analysis #2).

span.label: injury etiology (traumatic vs nontraumatic)
span.quote: As part of this analysis, we also assessed atrophy differences relating to injury etiology (ie, traumatic vs nontraumatic).

span.label: local subcortical atrophy measured by vertex shape analysis
span.term: local subcortical atrophy measured by vertex shape analysis
span.quote: To assess local brain atrophy on the basis of T1-weighted MR images, we employed a technique referred to as "shape (or vertex) analysis,"12 available in FMRIB Software Library (FSL).13

span.label: total normalized brain volume (head size)
span.quote: we calculated each subject’s total normalized brain volume using SIE- NAX19 and included this measure as a covariate in all analyses.

span.label: age and gender
span.quote: In the first analysis (ie, healthy volunteers vs patients), age, gender, and normalized brain volume were entered in the regression as covariates.

span.label: time since injury and recruiting center
span.term: time since injury and recruiting center
span.quote: (ie, all patient-only analyses), time since injury, etiology, and center (ie, Lie`ge, Cambridge) were additionally included as covariates.

span.label: 143 — consecutive patients with disorders of consciousness recruited
span.quote: In this cross-sectional study, we recruited a consecutive sample of 143 patients who survived severe brain injury and developed a disorder of consciousness.

span.label: 96 — healthy volunteers providing control images
span.quote: Control data were obtained for 96 healthy volunteers (51 female), ranging from 18 to 80 years of age

span.label: 28 — patient datasets discarded for low image quality before any analysis
span.quote: As described in the data preprocessing section below, 28 patient data sets were discarded because of low image quality (eg, in-scanner motion).

span.label: 115 / 38 / 63 / 14 — patients analysed, split into vegetative state, minimally conscious state and emerging-from-MCS
span.quote: Of the remaining 115 patients (61 from Cambridge and 54 from Lie`ge), 38 met the diagnostic criteria for VS (18 from Cambridge and 20 from Lie`ge), as evaluated with the CRS-R, 63 met the diagnostic criteria for MCS (37 from Cambridge and 26 from Lie`ge), and the 14 remaining met the criteria for eMCS (6 from Cambridge and 8 from Lie`ge; see Table 1).

span.label: 90% — total variance in the CRS-R subscales explained by the four retained PCA components
span.quote: The PCA returned 4 components, which collectively explained 90% of the total variance.

span.label: 100% and 99% — proportion of right and left globus pallidus vertices showing significant atrophy in patients versus volunteers
span.quote: extensive atrophy was detected in globus pallidus (100% and 99% of vertices in the right and left meshes, respectively), putamen (96% and 94% of vertices), hippocampus (93% and 95% of vertices), thalamus (97% and 88% of vertices).

span.label: 47% — share of patients whose injury was nontraumatic
span.quote: As shown in Table 1, about half the patients suffered from a traumatic brain injury, 47% suffered from nontraumatic brain injury, and the remaining 3% suffered from a mixed etiology.

span.label: 56% of vertices — extent of left thalamus showing extra atrophy in nontraumatic relative to traumatic injury
span.quote: nontraumatic injury was still associated with increased atrophy within the lateral and medial sections of left thalamus (56% of vertices), as well as a very small section of the left basal forebrain (1% of vertices), as compared to traumatic brain injury (see Fig 3B).

span.label: 84% vs 9.6% and 6% — proportions of bilateral, left- and right-lateralised injuries in the sample, used to rule out a trivial explanation of the left-lateralised thalamic finding
span.quote: which according to the clinical notes were mostly bilateral (84% vs 9.6% and 6% of left- and right-lateralized injuries, respectively).
